visualReview.notes: Inspected all9 final portable views against the actual owner ground photographs and aerial image. The pale pink tapered tower, octagonal ivory pedestal, fourteen staggered green windows, four upper vents, triangular pediments, southwest entrance and three steps, two gallery decks, lantern cage/ladder, green cap and full vane are present. The original detailed source is reproduced without a geometry change. Cached photograph filenames were checked against actual pixels; the image called california-day is the aerial reference.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected all9 final shared-material views including actual north-up driveway controls. Five canonical256px graphs provide lime plaster, limestone, painted metal, granite and plain wood. Green joinery and cap use shared surfaces with vertex tints; the window backing stays opaque. Every graph is read once; unloading leaves zero live model geometries. No embedded images or redistributed owner photographs. The actual road appears northeast of the tower in the geographic view and is an open driveway control, not a fabricated footprint.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected all24 final browser frames with sky reflections: noon/late light, economy/high settings, synthetic cottage context, four near cameras, district whole tower, street openings/entrance and four level transitions. Every level retains the full tower, green cap/vane, pedestal and southwest steps. Skyline represents fourteen windows and four vents with dark patches; district and nearer levels have actual recessed and backed apertures. District uses sixteen tapered facets and sparse gallery rails; street uses thirty-two segments, visible at its intended intermediate distance. Close-up preserves the original detailed source. No primary mass is missing.

limitations: The modeled exterior follows the cited published facts and inspected photographs. Unpublished dimensions and local fittings are explicitly photo-proportioned; no claim of engineering survey accuracy is made.
Portable PBR and shared metric surfaces are provided. Surface weathering, material color under local lighting and fine facade relief require close render review before maximum-detail acceptance.

The owner’s restored2016 exterior is modeled, including pale rose rather than the earlier strongly yellow paint. Diameter, moldings and trim are photo-proportioned; no secondary claim of a7.5m lantern diameter is accepted because it conflicts with the owner photographs. The30m navigation-list height excludes the thin weather-vane extension. Detached restaurant and site landscaping remain map features.
